With the fountain in sight, the party was assailed by ghostly spirits of drowned heroes who had lost themselves within the pools. After taking care of their attackers, each member of the party took a single drink from the fountain and soon fell asleep.

They awoke in a dark cave, with dwarven miners all around them. Then, from the opposite side of the huge cavern, a colossal earth titan burst forth. Surveying their surroundings, one of the party members pointed out that much of the equipment bore the symbol of Stonehold, the dwarven city state that they had defended from Dolghast, and the same city that Atrios and his leonin tribe saved from a titan nearly 400 years ago. Then, Bathoz had an epiphany. Somehow, they were reliving Atrios’ battle with the titan below the city of Stonehold. 

A hard battle was fought, with Soraya displaying many of her new combat skills, and our heroes defeated the mighty earth titan, with Davynn’s Meteor Swarm spell providing the killing blow. The titan released a burst of energy as its body fell apart, and Bathoz held his sword aloft and harnessed its immense magical power, finally attuning the sword to the plane of Ysgard. 

## [[Soraya's Resurrection]]

After returning to the village where they had first entered Ysgard, the party was able to convince Soraya to allow them to resurrect her. She made them promise to kill Kyron for what he did to her, and to not allow him to claim the lives of any more innocent people. After some heartfelt goodbyes between Soraya and her late father, Lucas, the party planeshifted back to Mudbend, where our tale first began. There, they left Soraya to tend to a few things and teleported back to Whitehall. They were met with unfortunate news.

## [[The Harbinger's Reprisal]]

Sitting on the steps in front of their mansion was Sebastion, the young tiefling sorcerer and oldest of the orphaned children that resided in the mansion with their caretaker, Harold. While the party had been in Ysgard, the Harbinger visited their mansion in the night. He came through the door, cut down Harold and his sister Patrice, then cast a powerful spell on Morbach, killing him instantly while bringing his corpse back as an undead creature. The Harbinger then left, allowing the undead Morbach to finish off the orphans. By some stroke of luck, Sebastion happened to be home that day, as he usually stayed at the local magic university. With tears streaming down his face, he explained to the party that he set the undead Morbach ablaze with his own spell, no doubt saving the lives of all the children, including Morbach’s own daughter Naori. Thankfully, none of the other children heard the sounds of fighting, and Sebastion was able to get some guards to come watch the house until the party returned a few days later.

Sebastian blamed Diggory and the rest of the party for dragging everyone else through their troubles. They may be saving the world, but they leave a wake of destruction behind them. Realizing it was a terrible idea to try to get under the Harbinger’s skin, Diggory vowed to be more cautious going forward, and then set about resurrecting Harold and Patrice. Resurrecting Morbach would be more difficult, being that he had been brought back as an undead creature already. Such a feat of restorative magic would require the True Resurrection spell, and carry with it the hefty price of 25,000 gold worth of diamonds. Diggory gathered the requirements, brought Morbach back, explained what had happened, and profusely apologized to Harold, Patrice, Morbach, and Sebastion. Harold wanted to leave the mansion, but did not have the heart to abandon the children. He did, however, ask for a raise. 

## [[Into the Beastlands]]

The party spent a few days of downtime and collecting supplies for their next interplanar journey - into the wild and feral Beastlands. Once ready, they teleported back to the home of Raiorma, the ancient amethyst dragon whose mate they saved from the Yuan-Ti on the Unclaimed Isle, as her village was only a few hours travel from the planar gate to the Beastlands. After a short journey, they neared the gate, only to find no life larger than the tiniest insects and frogs within two miles of it. Even more unnerving, the bones of a colossal dinosaur lay picked completely clean nearby. 

Using Bathoz’s sword as a sort of radar, the group ventured beneath a large stone temple and confronted a hive of mutated wasps that had been feeding off the planar gate’s energy to grow in both size and intelligence. After a tough fight, the group pressed on and through the portal.

The heroes found themselves in an even darker and more oppressively warm jungle than the Unclaimed Isle. With thick fog blocking much of their view, they wandered through the greenery, and soon found themselves ambushed by intelligent velociraptors. They dealt with the threat, and even met a tyrannosaurus rex couple who offered to share some of their meal, before reaching the edge of a massive plateau several thousand feet above a wide open grassland below. In the distance, seemingly dozens of miles away if not even further, stood a tree so tall it reached into the clouds. There was a lone side that pointed out in the direction of the tree, pointing the way to the only settlement in the entire plane, the village of Signpost. 

Using various forms magic, the group safely floated down to the grasslands and began flying atop Diggory who transformed himself into a mighty gold dragon. They spotted an immense flying castle in the skies above, before the sun was blocked by an imposing shadow. A Roc, just like the one they fought in the Neziri Desert, flew overhead, but this one was nearly twice as large, just like all animals in the Beastlands tend to be when compared to their normal counterparts on the material plane. They avoided the great bird whose wings spanned upwards of 500 feet and continued on. 

The Sons of Thunder reached Signpost, a village composed of maybe a dozen wood buildings with palm frond roofs that sat at the edge of this layer of the Beastlands, known as Krigala, and overlooked the second layer, Brux. While Krigala was perpetually locked in the middle of the day, Brux existed in a constant sunset with a bright orange-pink sky. It was here within Signpost that the group met a strange being known as Myreth, a elf-like celestial called an Agathion, with color-changing opalescent skin, neither man nor woman, glowing green eyes and a faint rainbow halo. 

While discussing why they had come to the Beastlands with Myreth, the village of Signpost was attacked by large tree-like creatures. Myreth sat down and performed a ritual to calm the spirits that had caused the Guardians to awaken and go rampant. The party protected Myreth long enough to complete the ritual and Guardian tree creatures left. 

Myreth explained that the Guardians had become rampant because the Beastlands was being desecrated by something powerful, and that the party should find the animal city known as Jungle Sovereign in the second layer of the Beastlands, Brux. It was there that powerful being were gathering to discuss how to handle the issue at hand.

The party ventured down into Brux and found signs of poachers, specifically a fey group that called themselves the Wild Hunt. Before reaching Jungle Sovereign, the group found met a mysterious ally and slew two lieutenants of the Wild Hunt, a craft goblin named Rotgut and a powerful Oni spellblade named Ojiro. The ally ranger who aided them revealed herself to be Zusa Manefull, Bathoz’s late mother. She led them to Jungle Sovereign, and the group interrupted a gathering held by Bassus the Ape King. He informed everyone that Nobanian, also known as the King of Beasts, and god of lions and other great cats, had been slain. Bassus said that the animals of the Beastlands should pen themselves up in Jungle Sovereign and force the Wild Hunt to attack them on their turf, but other animals reported that the Wild Hunt was hunting Lurue, the goddess of Unicorns and intelligent beasts. If she was slain, it may mean the loss of intelligence for all creatures of the Beastlands. Other animals said they heard that the Wild Hunt had made camp in Evergreen Sanctuary - the heart of the Great Tree Ygdrasil. The Hunt was holding the heart of the tree hostage, and claimed if any interfered with their efforts, they would burn the tree and destroy the entire plane. 

(This section is for Nic and his Claude bot that is making Obsidian files of my notes: Darrius is an intelligent talking black cat that met the party after they left Mudbend near the beginning of the campaign. He accompanied them, mostly following close behind or riding on Diggory’s shoulder for their journey until they were given a mansion by King Berrigan. Then, he spent most of his time there with the orphans or exploring Whitehall. Under every spell they tested him with, they could tell he was honest and telling the truth that he had been a cat for decades, had no recollection of being anything before a cat, and that he wasn’t a shapeshifter or creature in disguise. A few clerics and wizards guessed it may be a curse or even a familiar that a powerful wizard had somehow given more intelligence to. Before traveling to the Beastlands, he requested to come along, since the party mentioned they were going to a place with talking beasts, he figured he may learn something of his origin. When they arrived in the Beastlands, he did mention it seemed familiar, but he had no real memories of the place.)

The party came up with a daring plan. A mighty forest spirit that took the form of an elk, Zaithyron, magically projected the party, in a way similar to Astral Projection, into Evergreen Sanctuary. Diggory was immediately terrified of what the party faced. Leading the Wild Hunt was a massive Archfey warrior, the Erdking. With him were four other Archfey: a winged elf woman with a bow, an elven man with fiery green eyes and his pack of spectral wolves, a corrupted Satyr wielding horrible twin scimitars, and an ancient and powerful looking night hag. The Erdking was at first curious who these strangers were, but he soon noticed the sword Loryn wielded (his family heirloom sword that was recovered from Melvin, a blade of crystal called Razor’s Grace). The Erdking asked how Loryn came by the blade, which Loryn explained belonged to his grandfather. The Erdking also became visibly angry at the site of Darrius. He proposed a deal with the Sons of Thunder: they would have 24 hours to run from, hide from, or fight off the Wild Hunt. They could go anywhere in the Beastlands, but could not flee to other planes. If they could evade capture, the Hunt would leave forever. But if all members of the party were caught, the party had to give the Erdking Loryn’s sword, give him Darrius, and leave the Wild Hunt to continue their hunting. The Erdking said he would give the party one hour to prepare and then the hunt would begin. The party agreed.

Knowing their own strength, the group decided to seek powerful allies who could help them set up a defensible position somewhere and stave off the Hunt for 24 hours. A werebear who was at the meeting in Jungle Sovereign suggested they seek out Ursis, the good-hearted god of werebears, in his nearby realm of Balador. On their way to Ursis, they were attacked by the night hag woman from the Wild Hunt, who was revealed to be Malivorna, the daughter of Baba Yaga, one of the strongest spellcasters in history, and perhaps the mightiest living hag. She summoned two demons and a shadow clone of Davynn who attacked the party with powerful magic, but they slew her. From her corpse they recovered some items, including the fabled Demonomicon of Malivorna. The party knew they’d need it when they went to the Abyss.

They made it to the realm of Ursis, and with the help of many werebears and three Otter River Deities (Lord Vermilion Stoneriver - Guardian of the Crimson Beds, Lady Azura Shellstream - Keeper of the Sapphire Waters, Lord Viridian Greencreek - Sentinel of the Emerald Shores), the party staged a trap in a narrow canyon for the Hunt. Two of the evil archfey led a small army into the canyon, the winged elf archer Prascilia, and Vilerrus The Mad Dog, along with his pack of wolves. The River Deities caused a flood and wiped out many of the Hunt, and the party and werebears ambushed Vilerrus, who was forced to flee. Prascilia proved to be a difficult task, as she could fire deadly arrows from hundreds of feet above them. It took the might of Ursis the werebear god to draw her attention away from the party, who fled to the third layer of the Beastlands, Karasuthra.

Karasutha existed in perpetual moonlit night. Desperately tired, the party sought Lurue, the goddess of Unicorns, hoping she could aid them in a stand against the Erdking. Before they reached her, they were attacked by the wicked Satyr archfey, Gaidus - the Laughing Shadow. Turning invisible and striking from the shadows with his scimitar, it was a hard fight, but the party cornered and slew him, taking his blade, Hope’s Demise. 

Finally they reached Lurue’s realm and were greeted, then healed to their full strength by Lurue. She offered to stand with them against the Erdking, as she knew they would need her if they were going to live. Diggory used the spell Temple of the Gods to create a fortress temple. There, the Erdking would be forced to fight in a contained environment and pass through many traps before facing them. Prepared as they could be within the temple to Torm, they waited. 

The Erdking came like a storm, obliterating the door to the temple and marching in alone. The party peppered him with ranged attacks and spells, but he was seemingly unstoppable. The party had to avert their eyes as they fought him or steadily lose their ability to fight back under his crippling gaze. But, thanks to solid planning, some luck, and the aid of Lurue, they weakened him until he was forced to take his true form: Cerrunos, god of hunting and savagery. His very presence blew out all lights, even divine light, in the temple. Jakel, Bathoz, Diggory, and Loryn were all extremely wounded, but Davynn was finally able to strike the killing blow with True Telekinesis. 

With the Erdking dead, the remaining members of the Wild Hunt swore to honor the deal and leave the Beastlands in peace. Lurue gave a great deal of her divine power to attune Queensbane to the Beastlands, bringing the sword to 2/6ths of the way to being fully powered and able to defeat Aeralath. But, there was another surprise. By killing the Erdking, the party broke the curse that had been placed on Darrius. The black cat Darrius was transformed and revealed to be Abrovand, the King of Fools, the Lord of Pranks and Guile, the Jester in Red Green and Gold, or his official title - Archfey of Trickery and Illusions. He explained that he had been a friend of the Erdking for a lifetime, but when the Erdking first mentioned wanting to come to the Beastlands for hunting and pillaging 50 years ago, he knew it was wrong. He tricked the Erdking, stole the crystal blade Razor’s Grace, and lured him away from the Beastlands to the Material plane. It was there that Abrovand gave the sword to a kind man who aided him in his flight from the Erdking, Johan Malcovitch, Loryn’s grandfather (who said he won the sword in a duel). The Erdking finally caught up to Abrovand, who did not have the sword, and he cursed Abrovand, turning him into a cat, before returning to the Feywild until he could reach the Beastlands again. 

Abrovand swore to always aid the Sons of Thunder should they need it, and that he would always know them as true friends and brothers for saving him. He returned to the Feywild but promised to regularly return to Whitehall in the form of Darrius and check in on the orphans. The party then returned to the material plane.

## [[Into Mechanus]]

After some much needed downtime, the party set off on their third extraplanar excursion. This time, they were headed for the Clockwork Nirvana of Mechanus. The gate to Mechanus lay in Gudjag Canyon, home of the same Red Orcs that now served Jakel and had once served the Vampire Lord of War Ogzuuk Torah’kor. Near the gate, the party met a withered old red orc woman, a devout priestess of Gruumsh, god of orcs. She was nearly blind, and claimed she alone was the sole surviving red orc who was loyal to Gruumsh, and that a great champion called the Eye of Gruumsh guarded the strange ruins where the party knew the gate lay. She led them to the ruins, openly telling the party that the Eye would kill them for the glory of Gruumsh, and there the party was stunned to see the “Eye of Gruumsh” was in fact a massive metal construct with a singular eye in its chest. The construct was a Marut, an ultra powerful lawful creature loyal only to Primus, and referred to itself as Astynom Alpha 009. The intelligent construct said it would allow the party to enter Mechanus only if they first handed over their weapons, including Queensbane, first. Obviously, the party said no, and a fight ensued. 

Astynom Alpha 009 knocked Loryn out cold and promptly teleported both of them away. Having no choice but to assume the creature had taken Loryn to Limbo, the party stepped through the gate and found themselves immediately confronted by dozens of powerful Modrons within the supercity of Regulus, home to well over 350 million modrons. This time the party chose not to fight, and presented their reason for coming to Mechanus to the Modron interplanar customs, which took well over a full day of paperwork and interviews. Meanwhile, Loryn was being interrogated in a Modron prison, but was eventually released to his friends before all of them were ordered to meet with the Secundi, the Modrons who report directly to Primus. The three Secundi told the party they knew why they had come to Mechanus, and that they would aid the party in the final battle against Aeralath, but they needed the party to help them first. One of the four Secundi had gone rogue and taken an entire quarter of the Modron army with him. Without those forces, the Modron forces would not be at their full strength. Each of the Secundi governed an aspect of reality in Mechanus, space, matter, energy, and time. The rogue Secundi was Chronus, lord of time. The remaining three Secundi asked the party to find and slay Chronus. They said that Chronus believed he could turn back time to ensure Aeralath’s defeat and the salvation of the universe, but if such a thing was done it would tear reality apart from the inside out. He had taken refuge in the far reaches of Mechanus, past the edge of Modron controlled space, past a great expanse of unruled scraps and broken machinery called the Wastes of Gravegear, or the Scrapland. 

The party boarded a Magnodrone (living train Modron that travels along a rail) to take them to a factory called the Salvatorium that sits at the edge of Modron space. On the train, the party was ambushed by rogue Modrons, and was forced to fight from train car to train car, sometimes on the roof of the fast-moving train, and managed to keep the train from derailing. They arrived at the Salvatorium and found it abandoned, as if it had been attacked. In the office of the factory’s foreman, a high-ranking Quinton Modron, they found a notebook that mentioned a powersource known as the Lifeblood. The book detailed it as a silvery white magical fluid that all modrons are born of, and that it was an incredible power source, but unstable in many environments. It also reported exposing Lifeblood to unstable elements could lead to objects coming to life. 

The foreman hypothesized that similar magics could allow fleshbound organisms like humans or elves to transcend their material bodies without the use of necromancy and pass on into constructed forms, but such magic strictly violated the “Divine Edict of Forbidden Magics”, a term the party was not familiar with but sounded very important. They left the office, fought a massive rogue forge Modron and some liquid metal oozes brought to life by Lifeblood spilling into molten slag, but made their way through the factory and into the Wastes of Gravegear. 

Like all of Mechanus the wastes sat atop massive, sometimes continent-sized, everturning gears. The wastes were seemingly endless, functioning as a universal junkyard, as the party found remnants of technologies and civilizations from across time and many different planes of existence. They fought off elite goblinoid junk raiders aboard airships from the neighboring plane of Acheron, giant scrap monsters creatures possessed by ghosts, and even had to stave off a form of junkyard madness that made Bathoz want to walk around naked. A storm of tiny metal shards forced them to seek shelter under a mountain of debris, where they stumbled across an unlikely group of stranded beings from across the universe. All the people in the underground “village” were clearly insane, including a Balor who liked to bake, a strange aberration seemingly made of living wood, a fallen angel who escaped Modron prison, a man with the head of a donkey who always wore an unsettling smile, and an elderly human wizard named Qadus Ifnir. 

As it turns out, Qadus was the previous owner of the mansion the party now owned in Whitehall. He had accidentally disappeared through a portal to Mechanus he opened during an experiment in the mansion’s basement a few years ago. The party realized that Qadus and the other crazed villagers would not let them leave, and tensions steadily rose until a fight broke out. After a surprisingly tough fight, the party slew the odd crew of lost souls and ventured further across the wastes until they reached a fork in the road. They had to choose between crossing myconid controlled territory or formian territory. Not wanting to deal with mushroom people, the party chose to deal with the formians, even though none of them knew what a formian was.

Trekking across Formian territory into the unknown, the party quickly came face to face with formians, highly intelligent and psionically gifted ant-beings that ranged in size from 3 to 7 feet tall. The party explained they aimed to stop Chronus, so the formians brought the party before their queen, the Hive Mother - Queen Regent Chitinousa, at the bottom of an inverted tower-like termite mound structure that hung thousands of feet below the giant gear.

Chitinousa gave her blessing to the party, and commanded her Formian warriors to clear a path through Chronus’s army of rogue Modrons so that the party could destroy him. She also sent one of her finest warriors, a fighter named Theh Kha, to aid them in the fight against Chronus.

With the aid of the Formians, the party reached Chronus, in his realm of twisted and distorted time in the ruins of a crumbling clock tower. As the party made their way through the ruins, they saw visions of alternate timelines had they made different choices in their lives. Those visions are detailed here: 

Theh Kha: He chose to wait to embark on his warrior’s trial until he was of traditional age. Because of this, he became wounded in a battle with a rival hive before his trial. He lived out his days as a mundane attendant to the larvae. His short life passes, completely devoid of the glory he now craves. 

Bathoz: He chose not to challenge Kuzo, and thus stayed in the pride. He was present during the invasion by the Dragonborn. He ended up seeing Kuzo slain by Krintak, tried to fight back, and was killed. The Leonin people became enslaved and the Dragonborn rule the plains.

Davynn: He chose to decline his brother’s magical duel. Mocked as a coward for declining, he applied himself to his studies with vengeance as his motive, and gained vast arcane knowledge quite quickly. But like a festering seed, his resentment toward his brother grew, and his heart darkened. Eventually, his teachers noticed his potential and word spread of his meteoric rise. Taking notice, the Harbinger became his master and led him to aid in Aeralath’s return.

Loryn: He chose to work with his brother in the “shipping” industry. Things started off well, spending more time than ever with his brother. But over time, he steadily became desensitized to bigger and bigger red flags. Not willing to break his parent’s hearts by revealing that he and Melvin are criminals, he went on with his schemes as a passive participant in his awful plans. A full member of the Ashen Saints, Loryn eventually turned on his brother, his conscience forcing him to, but he was no match for Melvin and his men. He is slain by Melvin. 

Diggory: He chose to stay in the woods of Loradris instead of seeking adventure. His days were spent full of herbs and wine. Until one day he went on a trip with Prim and found himself at the Eldergleam, where they were captured by bizarre fiends. There, he was tortured, corrupted into a fiendish mirror of himself, and turned against his own people. Diggory would aid in the destruction of his forest home, and laugh and revel in the pain would cause.

Jakel: He chose not to flee that fateful night when he found his mother and his castle was set on fire. He confronted his father, and Ifan revealed his plan. Ifan assumed the fire was started by those who knew he was a vampire. Ifan wanted to unify the country under his rule, and Jakel joined his family in their caused to unify the land under Ifan. He agreed to become a full vampire. Queen Marislova was slain, and Ifan took power. Then, Ifan managed to turn Golzokroth the Blood Tyrant into a vampiric greatworm. Golzokroth’s black fire breath turned the whole nation into an undead army. Jakel, Ifan, Melvin, and Kyron, help Dolghast rule the whole world. Then, the demons came. The world was easy pickings. Jakel’s vision ended with him kneeling to his lord, Orcus. 

The party finally found and faced off with Chronus who used his powers of time manipulation to great effect and gave the party an extremely difficult fight. Theh Kah provided the edge they needed to be victorious, but Davynn was nearly slain after Chronus struck him with a 9th level Time Ravage spell (aging him to within 30 days of dying of old age). Bathoz absorbed Chronus’s power into Queensbane, therein attuning the blade to Mechanus, before they teleported back to the city of Regulus. 

Safely back in the Modron city, the party was brought before Primus, Supreme God of Law and Lord over all Modrons. He expressed his greatest thanks to the party for eliminating Chronus, which in turn destroyed all rogue Modrons who reported to him. Those same Modrons would be remade by Primus from the endless pools of Lifeblood energy that he waded through. He also personally thanked Theh Kah by enhancing his wrist-mounted crossbow up to artifact-level power. They Kah requested to come to the Material Plane, as he was tired of life in the hive and wished to see what the rest of the world held for him. With one last reminder that his Modrons would be there to fight with mortal kind when the demons came, he sent the party back to the Material Plane. They arrived outside the gate to Mechanus in Gudjag Canyon, where they parted ways with Theh Kah, as he decided to explore this new world on his own. 

## [[The Slaying of Minthur]]

After a few days of rest in Whitehall, where they saw Abrovand in his cat/Darrius form for a bit, the party decided to take a bit of a detour before heading to Limbo for their fourth outer plane. The Sons of Thunder had already slain two of the hybrid dragons, Golzokroth and Rendibrïl. Convincing themselves it was to “protect the realm”, and not just because they wanted to let off some steam before heading to what would certainly be their most dangerous outer plane yet, the party decided to hunt down another hybrid dragon. They set their sights on the blue-green, or turquoise dragon: Minthur, the Mindbreaker. Their notes from Mathias Ohstal said that Minthur breathed a "psychedelic gas” for a breath weapon, and he could be found by a large waterfall that overlooked the Dreaming Jungle on the border of Rorinden and Isembard.

Davynn teleported the group to the Dreaming Jungle near Minthur’s lair. Once inside, they were ambushed by a high level tabaxi druid who claimed Minthur was guarding the Dreaming Jungle, the druid’s home, from being harvested for resources by the Isembard and Rorinden governments. The party did not listen and fought and slew the druid. Finding the druid’s makeshift home within the caves leading to Minthur’s personal lair, they found belongings that revealed the druid was named Viridian Sun, and was in fact the older brother of Jade Moon, a tabaxi bard they knew. They knew they should tell her what happened (they never did).

Delving further into the caves, the party slew a tribe of jungle trolls led by a mighty troll shaman before making it to Minthur’s sanctum within the larger cave system. Minthur’s lair was a high-ceiling cave with a hidden opening in the roof that he used to come and go at will (it was magically concealed from the outside). The rest of the lair was a single large cave with steep walls and only a few large rocks to stand on within a deep and fast-moving river that led to the waterfall by the cave system’s entrance. Working hard to swim against the current and find refuge on the rocks, the party was attacked from below by the waiting Minthur. While nowhere near as strong as Golzokroth, Minthur was prepared for the party and used the deep water for hit and run tactics, blasting them with gas that dealt psychic damage before diving underwater. He whittled the party down to low health before he was forced to flee. 

Minthur turned invisible and fled through the hole in the roof of the cave and vowed to kill as many innocents as he could to get back at the party for coming to his home unprovoked and looking for blood. He sped off to the southeast, seeking to destroy the city of Mushala. Diggory True Polymorphed into a dragon and a chase ensued. Loryn’s keen eyes were able to spot the trees being disturbed by Minthur’s wingbeats and the party was able to slay Minthur after Jakel was knocked unconscious. Without Loryn’s luck and sharp eyes, thousands of innocent lives would have been lost. 

Returning to Minthur’s lair, the party collected over 500,000 gold worth of coins, gems, art, and other magic items, some of which were quite powerful. But, none of
